topic: The Physics of Pi: Colliding Blocks and the Digits of π
target_audience: Undergraduate physics or computer science students with a basic understanding of momentum and conservation laws.

sections.title: Introduction: The Unexpected Appearance of π
animations: Create two block objects (color #3498DB for moving block, #E74C3C for stationary).
Animate moving block colliding with stationary block showing velocity exchange.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
animations: Show Momentum P = mv and Energy E = 0.5mv^2 labels (color #F1C40F).
Animate two particles exchanging momentum visually.

sections.title: Mapping Collisions to Geometry
animations: Plot phase space axes (color #95A5A6) and show current state as a Point (color #2ECC71).
Animate point trajectory reflecting off boundary lines (color #E67E22).
Highlight angle of reflection with an arc object (color #FFFFFF).
Draw the path trace revealing a circular arc.

sections.title: The Scaling Phenomenon: Why π?
animations: Animate multiple arc trajectories overlapping to form a circle.
Highlight intersection point (color #E74C3C, scale 0.5) showing π.
Animate geometric convergence towards a circular arc.

sections.title: Conclusion and Deep Intuition
animations: Animate a closing summary arc transitioning into a π symbol.
